sa-cavia-porcellus.title: Guinea Pig
sa-cavia-porcellus.summary: Social and long-lived, guinea pigs need another guinea pig for company, lots of hay and a daily source of vitamin C, since they can't make their own. They live longer than hamsters, gerbils, mice or rats.
rows: At least 10 sq ft (e.g. 5 × 2 ft) of single-level space; bigger is better. Paper bedding or hay rather than wood shavings. Keep warm and dry and avoid sudden temperature changes
Unlimited good-quality hay (most of the diet) plus grass when possible; fresh guinea-pig pellets daily for vitamin C; a daily rotation of vitamin-C-rich vegetables and herbs. Fruit only as a treat
Keep in pairs or groups: female pairs, male pairs (often siblings), or one neutered male with females. Do not house with rabbits
Domesticated in the Andes of South America
notes: Rabbits make their own vitamin C and guinea pigs do not, so the two cannot share the same diet (or housing).

sources.name: Humane World for Animals – Is a guinea pig the right pet for you?

sa-cavia-porcellus-skinny.title: Skinny Pig (Hairless Guinea Pig)
sa-cavia-porcellus-skinny.summary: An almost hairless guinea pig, with fur only on its muzzle, feet and legs. Skinny pigs need the same care as other guinea pigs, plus indoor housing, extra warmth and a bit more food to keep up their body heat.
rows: Indoors only, at least 10 sq ft single-level space, with soft nesting (a fleece or cloth bag) to stay warm. Protect the bare skin from sun and scrapes

Unlimited good-quality hay (most of the diet) plus grass when possible; fresh guinea-pig pellets daily for vitamin C; a daily rotation of vitamin-C-rich vegetables and herbs. Fruit only as a treat. Skinny pigs eat more than haired guinea pigs to stay warm
Keep in pairs or groups like other guinea pigs
Gentle; the bare skin is easily scratched
warn: Bare skin is prone to sunburn, injuries and fungal infections.
